items.summary: Publishing has always evolved alongside civilization. From handwritten manuscripts to the printing press, from digital publishing to Artificial Intelligence. Publishing has never been more accessible and becoming an author has never been easier. Becoming an authority, however, remains as difficult as ever. We have spent over three decades working with authors, professionals, experts and leaders enabling, guiding and helping them learn how books influence careers, and help professionals build strong personal brands, credibility, and thought leadership, in an increasingly crowded marketplace. items.title: HC can't grant relief if anticipatory bail plea premature: Supreme Court overturns relief to Sunil Biyani
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a Bombay High Court ruling protecting Future Group’s non-executive director Sunil Biyani from arrest in a ₹1,200-crore Goods and Services Tax (GST) scam [ Union of India v. Sunil Biyani ]. Notably, the High Court had granted this protection even though it held that Biyani's anticipatory bail application in the matter was premature, since the GST authorities had not passed any order under Section 69 (power to arrest) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act. In its February ruling, the High Court had directed that if any such order for Biyani's arrest is issued by the GST authorities, he should not be arrested for a week from the date of intimation of such order. The Central government challenged this ruling before the Supreme Court. It questioned whether High Courts possess inherent jurisdiction to grant interim protection from arrest to a litigant after holding that their anticipatory bail petition is premature and unmaintainable. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu today ruled that the manner in which protection from arrest was given by the High Court was impermissible. items.title: Can social media platforms suspend accounts based on copyright strikes? Delhi High Court to examine

The case will be heard next on September 24. items.title: Hens are 'livestock' under MV Act; owner can claim insurance for loss of hens in road accident: Karnataka HC
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that hens constitute 'livestock' under the Motor Vehicles Act and therefore, their loss in a road accident can be treated as damage to goods covered by a motor insurance policy [K Veera Narayana Swamy vs Y Yankappa] . Justice Geetha KB rejected Reliance General Insurance Company's argument that hens cannot be considered livestock. It was dealing with the insurer's challenge against the grant of compensation of ₹4.51 lakh by a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) to a poultry farm owner after his 2,000 broiler hens died in the road accident. "Livestock means and includes hens. Hence, the hen is considered as livestock" the Court said. It relied upon Section 2(13) of Motor Vehicles Act which states that ‘goods’ include livestock. Justice Geetha KB The poultry farm owner had earlier claimed compensation of ₹5.90 lakh in connection with the death of 2,250 broiler hens that were being transported in an Eicher van. The claimant said the vehicle overturned, resulting in the death of around 2,000 hens, while the remaining 250 were allegedly taken away by people from the neighbouring area. items.title: Threats not made up, boost his security: Delhi HC to government on Pappu Yadav's plea for enhanced security
items.summary: eaThe Delhi High Court on Tuesday ordered the Central government to immediately provide one more personal security officer (PSO) to Bihar independent Member of Parliament (MP) Pappu Yadav. Justice Manoj Jain said that the interim measure will stay in place till the government decides on Yadav's representation for an increase in his security. The Court also remarked that the concern raised by Yadav about his security has to be taken seriously. "There is something significant. He is the sitting MP. You boost his security... Despite being some adequate measures, some incident has taken place. Don’t say it [the attack] is made up," the Court remarked. Justice Manoj Jain In his plea, Yadav sought a fresh and comprehensive threat assessment and interim security measures across India. He currently has ‘Y+’ security cover in Bihar. Yadav had argued that he has been receiving death threats since he performed a skit outside the parliament over irregularities in the Ram Mandir donations. The plea stated that death threats were issued against him on August 1, including a public reward of ₹51 lakh for his beheading. items.title: Supreme Court declines relief to TMC in bank account freeze case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld Calcutta High Court's refusal to grant any interim relief to Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction in its plea challenging the freeze of its bank accounts by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale said the High Court passed a balanced order after taking note of the fact that party has sufficient funds available to run day-to-day affairs of the party. The Court said since the matter including a petition related to the freeze ordered on TMC's accounts by West Bengal Police is pending before High Court, any discussion on merits would not be appropriate. "We are not inclined to interfere in both the matters. Disposed of, " the Bench said. Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale of Supreme Court On the last hearing, the Court had sought ED’s response on whether a limited amount from the frozen bank accounts could be released to a court-appointed administrator to meet the party's day-to-day expenses. items.title: Dhruv Rathee video on Hindu deities eating meat withheld in India after Centre's order: Google tells Delhi HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court was informed on Tuesday that Dhruv Rathee's YouTube video - in which he allegedly said that Hindu gods Ram, Seeta and Krishna consumed meat and alcohol - has been withheld in India. Google's counsel told Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma that the step was taken after the government's Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC) passed the order. A GAC is a government-established body that allows users to appeal decisions made by social media platforms and other online intermediaries regarding complaints about online content or accounts. The GAC order came after Justice Sharma asked the government to decide Advocate Amita Sachdeva's plea flagging the content in 15 days. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma Sachdeva today told the Court that the video can still be viewed outside India and in the country using a VPN. She then asked for an order to remove the video globally. However, Google's counsel said that the issue of global removal of content is pending before the Division Bench of the High Court. items.title: Delhi High Court denies bail to wrestler Sushil Kumar in Sagar Dhankar murder case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently denied bail to two-time Olympic medallist Sushil Kumar in wrestler Sagar Dhankar's murder case. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said that it was a case of "a premeditated and gruesome assault resulting in death" and that a lot of material is yet to be tested at trial. The Court noted that the Supreme Court had raised concerns over Kumar's conduct before his arrest and that "his capacity to influence the outcome of the trial given his standing, have not been shown to have altered in any material particular". "In these circumstances, this Court is not persuaded that the petitioner has made out a case either for a genuine change in circumstances within the meaning of the liberty reserved by the Supreme Court, or, independently, for the grant of regular bail on the ordinary parameters governing Section 439 CrPC/ 483 BNSS. The application is, accordingly, dismissed," Justice Kaurav ordered. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav Kumar was denied bail by the trial court on February 6, 2026, in connection with the 2021 murder of junior wrestler Dhankar. items.title: View that women wearing jeans 'corrupts' boys unacceptable: Delhi HC overturns acquittal in sexual harassment case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently warned that a woman’s choice of clothing cannot be cited to justify sexual harassment against her. Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha made the observation while convicting a man for sexually harassing a 17 year-old-girl. Notably, the judge took critical note that one of the reasons cited for the acquittal was the failure of the police to look into the complaints made by the accused and fifty local residents against the prosecutrix and her mother. Justice Sudha was at a "loss of words" on finding that the alleged “crime” of the sexual assault victim and her mother was living in society without a male member, wearing western clothes, “corrupting” the minds of young boys in the locality, having questionable character and filing false complaints against “innocent boys” of the area. The Court observed that these "complaints" reflected a deeply troubling and unacceptable mindset. “What a girl or woman chooses to wear is a matter of her personal choice. items.title: US court accepts Trump government proposal to dismiss fraud charges against Gautam Adani but terms it "highly unusual"
items.summary: A United States court has dismissed securities and wire fraud charges against Indian industrialist and billionaire Gautam Adani and two other executives, bringing the criminal proceedings against them to an end. Judge Nicholas G Garaufis of the US District Court for the Eastern District of New York on August 11 accepted the proposal of the US Department of Justice (DOJ) to dismiss all three charges brought against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain - securities fraud conspiracy, wire fraud conspiracy and securities fraud. However, Judge Garaufis expressed concern about the manner in which the DOJ made the proposal and termed it "highly unusual". " The fact that McCotter came to this decision largely in collaboration with defense counsel, and seemingly without input from the FBI and SEC agents who investigated the alleged misconduct, or the attorneys from the Department, SEC, and U.S. Attorney’s Office who brought the case, appears to be highly unusual, " the order said. The Court's decision to drop charges comes after multiple affidavits were filed by Adani and DOJ over two months.
